subject: Preemptive eviction policy change — customer ops note & next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@starlite.ai>, Starlite Ops <ops@starlite.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 15:15:00 -0700
Subject: Preemptive eviction policy change — brief incident note

Hi Alex / Starlite Ops team —

Wanted to surface a short incident summary and the temporary measures we enabled earlier today. Between 10:30–11:05 PDT we observed a sustained surge in short-lived burst jobs in a subset of Redwood Dedicated GPU pools that caused aggressive queueing and eviction of lower-priority warm nodes. To stop cascading latency impact across shared tenancy and preserve throughput for heavyweight reserved customers we enabled a preemptive eviction policy for 35 minutes.

What we did (short):
- Enabled preemptive eviction flag on affected host group (grp-us-west-2-a-03).
- Rate-limited transient burst queues and rerouted noncritical low-priority jobs to fallback smaller-quantized model variants.
- Opened a high-priority incident and attached traces for immediate review (incident-summary-eviction-20260912.pdf).

Impact to Starlite AI: your Dedicated pool experienced 12 evictions of warm nodes and several 502/short-timeout errors for requests submitted during the window. We know this disrupted a small percentage of inference calls (roughly 0.8% of total tokens for the hour).

Next steps we are taking:
1) Immediate: pushing a targeted rollback of the eviction flag for your pool and reintroducing node weighting to prevent further churn. ETA rollback: ~2 hours.
2) Short-term: scheduling a 30-minute deep-dive with your ops to share traces and a focused mutual action plan.
3) Commitment: temporary credit offer for impacted consumption (proposed: 10% credit on the bill for the incident hour).

Attachments: incident-summary-eviction-20260912.pdf (summary + timeline).

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for a deep-dive tomorrow. Sorry for the disruption — we want to make this right and prevent recurrence.

—Dylan

Dylan Brooks
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Chen <alex@starlite.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Starlite Ops <ops@starlite.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preemptive eviction policy change — brief incident note

Dylan —

Thanks for the quick note. We saw elevated 502s and a small number of failed inferences; appreciate the transparency. A couple of asks so we can triage internally:
- Can you confirm which job classes were marked low-priority (batch vs realtime)?
- We need the raw eviction logs and KV-cache stats for the window for our SREs (preferably the GPU trace tarball).
- Please confirm the timeline and exact credit calculation.

We’re available for a deep-dive tomorrow at 10:00 PDT. Can you send a calendar invite?

—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform, Starlite AI
alex@starlite.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preemptive eviction policy change — brief incident note

Dylan / team —

Draft customer response and credit language below (feel free to edit). I recommend we: 1) approve the 10% incident credit for the hour, 2) provide the eviction + kv-cache logs, and 3) offer a one-week prioritized onboarding for a dedicated headroom plan (provision reserved spare node or pin quantized variant).

Suggested wording for external (short):
"We sincerely apologize for the disruption. During a short window our automated eviction policy engaged to protect overall cluster stability which resulted in brief timeouts for some requests. We have rolled back the temporary setting and will share logs and a remediation plan in a joint session. As a gesture we will apply a 10% credit for the impacted hour and prioritize a headroom allocation for the next 7 days while we complete a root-cause analysis."

Internal ops notes:
- Confirm that rollback is scheduled and executed once Marcus validates warm-cache warming metrics.
- Package GPU trace and runbook (runbook-tiered-fallback-v1.md) on shared Drive link.
- Prepare statement re: model-routing fallback (we switched some traffic to gpt-medium-int8 variants).

I’ll draft the calendar invite and the artifact bundle for Stack.

—Laura

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@starlite.ai>, Starlite Ops <ops@starlite.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Jake Porter <jake.porter@cloudpartner.io>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preemptive eviction policy change — brief incident note

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and the asks. Meeting invite sent for Tue 2026-09-14 10:00 PDT (30m).

Answers / artifacts attached:
- Which job classes: realtime inference sharded requests were marked low-priority for eviction; we avoided touching any reserved throughput jobs.
- Eviction logs + kv-cache stats: attached as gpu-trace-20260912.tar.gz (contains per-node eviction events, timestamps, and KV hit/miss histograms).
- Credit calculation: 10% credit applied to your usage during 10:30–11:30 PDT on 2026-09-12. Final credit will be visible on the invoice after billing cycle close.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Rolled back preemptive eviction on your pool at 11:40 PDT.
- Provisioned a temporary 2-slot reserved headroom for 72 hours to absorb bursts while we finalize the root cause remediation.

Attachments: gpu-trace-20260912.tar.gz, runbook-tiered-fallback-v1.md.

We’ll walk through the traces and proposed remediation during the deep-dive. If you prefer a different credit figure we can discuss during the call.

—Dylan

Dylan Brooks
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 17:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Post-rollback next steps and permanent mitigations

Team —

Quick internal summary after rollback and customer sync:
- Rollback confirmed at 11:40 PDT on 2026-09-12 (policy flag cleared).
- Root cause (preliminary): short TTLs on our transient-work queue allowed a burst pattern to disproportionately trigger eviction thresholds; combined with scheduler weight rounding on the host-group this created rapid churn.
- Temporary measures we implemented: 72h headroom reservation for Starlite, 10% credit, immediate runbook to prefer quantized fallback models for transient jobs.

Permanent work items (owners / ETA):
- Scheduler weight fix to remove rounding edge-case (owner: infra-scheduler team; ETA: 2026-10-05).
- Improve detection heuristics to distinguish ephemeral burst vs sustained workloads and avoid preemptive eviction (owner: runtime team; ETA: 2026-09-28).
- Add a customer-safe grace period to eviction logic (owner: serving runtime; ETA: 2026-10-12).

I’ll attach the incident ticket INF-9821 and we’ll run a full RCA next week. Laura, please confirm customer messaging is closed out; Dylan, please confirm credits are applied through billing.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
